title: Schedule the Nightly Backup
description: Create a cron job that runs the backup script every night at 02:00 as root.
scenario: The ops runbook requires nightly configuration backups at 02:00. The backup script itself is ready at /usr/local/bin/backup.sh — what is missing is the schedule. Create /etc/cron.d/nightly-backup with a valid cron entry that runs the script as root every day at 02:00. Remember: /etc/cron.d files need the username field that plain crontabs don't have.
symptoms: No cron file references the backup script
The runbook requires 02:00 nightly, as root
The job must live in /etc/cron.d/nightly-backup (config-managed, survives reboots)

hints.title: The five time fields
hints.content: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week — `0 2 * * *` means 02:00 every day. Stars mean 'every'.

hints.title: cron.d needs a username
hints.content: Unlike a personal crontab, every /etc/cron.d line names the USER the job runs as, right after the schedule: `0 2 * * * root /usr/local/bin/backup.sh` — seven fields total (5 time fields + username + command).

hints.title: tee for root files
hints.content: `echo ... | sudo tee /etc/cron.d/nightly-backup` writes a root-owned file from your shell.

acceptance_criteria.description: every active line has the 7 fields /etc/cron.d requires (5 time fields + username + command)
the schedule line is exactly '0 2 * * * root /usr/local/bin/backup.sh'
the scheduled backup script is executable
